messages.subject: Closing polygons in polar coordinates
parts:
Hi everyone,

I want to plot wind roses in ggplot which look like
http://addictedtor.free.fr/graphiques/RGraphGallery.php?graph=123

I have pre-summarised data that looks like this:
angle value
0.0 4.4658494
22.5 1.2259194
...
315.0 4.3782837
337.5 4.5534151
which I plotted using an area plot in polar coordinates
d <- structure(list(angle = c(0, 22.5, 45, 67.5, 90, 112.5, 135, 157.5,
180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5), value = c(4.465849387,
1.22591944, 1.22591944, 1.663747811, 1.663747811, 0.963222417,
1.838879159, 3.327495622, 4.028021016, 0.963222417, 0.788091068,
0.175131349, 0.963222417, 1.576182137, 4.378283713, 4.553415061
)), .Names = c("angle", "value"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
16L))
ggplot(d) + geom_area(aes(x=angle, y=value)) +
coord_polar() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,360))

The problem is that the last angle is quite far from the first (337.5
-> 0) and this causes a gap in the shape, evidenced by:
ggplot(d) + geom_path(aes(x=angle, y=value)) +
coord_polar() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,360))
while I would want it to be closed (i.e. join the last data to the first).

I think this use case is probably pretty common for polar coordinate
plots in which x is actually an angle: 0 and 360 are the same and
should be joined. It is a matter of
adding an extra point which is the first + 2*pi
add <- d[which.min(d$angle),]
add$angle <- add$angle + 360
d <- rbind(d, add)
ggplot(d) + geom_path(aes(x=angle, y=value)) +
coord_polar() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,360))

However, I am still wondering how general this would be. I think for
geom_area, ribbon, polygon, density it is safe to do assume people
expect it but I don't see a mechanism to change the behaviour of a
coord based on the geom in use. Maybe the safest way would be a "join"
option to coord_polar()

As a starting point, I tried to modifying coord_polar()

diff --git a/R/coord-polar.r b/R/coord-polar.r
index 494092d..7d3de76 100644
--- a/R/coord-polar.r
+++ b/R/coord-polar.r
@@ -72,7 +72,13 @@ CoordPolar <- proto(Coord, {
data <- within(data, {
r <- .$r_rescale(r, details)
theta <- .$theta_rescale(theta, details)
+ })
+
+ addRow <- data[which.min(data$theta),]
+ addRow$theta <- addRow$theta + 2*pi
+ data <- rbind(data, addRow)

+ data <- within(data, {
x <- r * sin(theta) + 0.5
y <- r * cos(theta) + 0.5
})

but this throws an error when plotting:
> ggplot(d) + geom_area(aes(x=angle, y=value)) + coord_polar() +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,360))
Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
arguments imply differing number of rows: 1552, 1551
1552 is much more than the number of lines of my data.frame. So I am
assuming this is after munching. I just could not track it down (proto
and debug() are not good friends, nor proto and I).

I would appreciate suggestions on the way forward.

Thanks,

JiHO
